details: False for the catalogue conventions: best mistakes uses a favorable order of the whole domain, whereas self-directed complexity maximizes over coordinate subsets. Private-coordinate cubes have $M_{\mathrm{best}}=1$ and $M_{\mathrm{sd}}=d$ for $d\ge2$.
witness_verification: The survey gives the all-d argument: private indicators give whole-domain mistake cost one; the cube-coordinate restriction forces d self-directed mistakes, and every subset has cost at most d. The former blockwise-addressing witness did not justify the universal inequality under the changed self-directed convention.
name: Best Mistakes / Self-Directed Queries Complexity
proof_source: Companion survey, private-coordinate cube example (ex:private-cube-mistake-separation). The fixed-set simulation remains valid in lem:fixed-set-mistake-comparison.
